analysis.title: Traders Look To Wall Street Quant Bets For Hedges
key_insights: After the US midterm elections, investors are hedging against two scenarios: an overdone market response to the Democratic sweep of Congress, and a deeper, broader retreat in AI stocks.

The S&P 500 fell 4.4% on Thursday. Prime brokers reported lower gross and net leverage going into the midterms, and financing costs are well below the summer peak, which points to reduced demand for borrowing to add positions.
Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage data show global hedge fund gross leverage down 8% from June through October. After Thursday, US hedge fund net leverage fell to the bottom 10% of readings since 2010.

Bank client conversations center on crash protection with zero carry cost. QIS (quantitative investment strategies) research is going into what some call targeted convexity, including macro-trigger timing and volatility momentum signals built on intraday data.

Premialab data show systematic short volatility performing well over the long term. Selling VIX call spreads had the best carry across providers and outperformed various dispersion tactics popular with hedge funds.

Premialab's CEO sees interest in combining vol carry with protection to offset hedging cost. He attributes VIX call spread carry to the premium embedded in VIX options, demand for volatility protection and the pricing of vol-of-vol risk.
QIS performance depends on when a trade is opened and closed, so a reliable timing signal matters. Long 0DTE puts are one example where intraday timing makes a large difference to results.

UBS partnered with One River Switzerland for long-volatility timing signals that have been live for more than 10 years with capital behind them. UBS notes signal-based strategies can lose effectiveness out of sample.

Single-stock volatility contracted in July-August and dispersion P&L drew down. Several systematic dispersion baskets recovered during earnings season. JPMorgan's US Technology Gamma Dispersion Index was up more than 6% over the past year, even through Thursday's slide.
Custom single-name dispersion baskets concentrated in tech-heavy names are a popular theme. They let investors keep exposure to high-conviction names while adding protection in a correction.

The next step for dispersion QIS may be a timing signal for the short index volatility leg. With indexes moving 5% on little news, selling index volatility to fund long single-stock volatility is hard. Strategies may shift toward outright long single-stock volatility in stress, adjusting as correlations rise.

Many hedge funds are positioning for a grind lower rather than a crash, which explains the popularity of spot down/volatility down trades. JPMorgan flags investor focus on shallow hedges such as systematic down-and-out puts, which protect against moderate selloffs for about half the premium of a vanilla put.

tension_points.bull_case: Dispersion baskets recovered during earnings season, and JPMorgan's US Technology Gamma Dispersion Index was up more than 6% over the past year, even through Thursday's slide.
tension_points.bear_case: With indexes moving 5% on little news, selling index volatility to fund long single-stock volatility becomes a daunting proposition, and strategies may shift to outright long single-stock volatility as correlations rise.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Indexes gyrating by 5% on seemingly little news, which would break the short index volatility leg of conventional dispersion trades.
